To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proposed holistic representation of the visual content of a natural scene in the discrete-cosine transform domain is a powerful tool for scene classification, which can be exploited in constrained domain, and that the proposed representation is able to outperform state-of-the-art holistic representations in terms of accuracy and computational resources.
we propose a novel method to perform scene classification in compressed and in constrained domain, and the obtained results are very promising.

we propose a holistic representation of natural scenes in the DCT domain fully compatible with JPEG format and that we demonstrate the effectiveness of the representation for scene classification at different levels of description (e. g. natural versus artificial or portrait, landscape and documents).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: (1) the development of holistic representation of the image content; (2) the development of a classification system for the scene classification task.
the following aspects of scene classification: (1) scene classification in compressed domain; (2) scene classification in constrained domain; (3) scene classification in the presence of noise.

the development of a new holistic representation of natural scenes in a constrained domain, which is able to work at the same time on a compressed representation of the image and on the JPEG compressed image.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a good candidate for real-world applications, such as scene classification in compressed domain.
the proposed method is a promising approach to perform holistic scene classification in compressed and/or constrained domain.
the proposed method is able not only to perform classification of scenes but also to work with compressed and constrained images.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to perform holistic scene classification in compressed domain and with very low computational resources.
the holistic representation of the image in the frequency domain, coupled with a logistic regression classifier, can achieve high accuracy for scene classification with a low computational cost.
we have proposed a novel method for scene classification in constrained domain that can be applied to a wide range of imaging systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed method can be used as a pre-processing step to perform a first scene classification before the decoding process, thus reducing the computational load and the memory required by the decoding process.
the proposed method can be easily implemented on the consumer imaging device to perform classification of scene content.
the proposed method can be used to provide a holistic representation of natural scenes in the frequency domain, fully compatible with the standard JPEG image format, to be used in consumer devices.
